claim: Skeletal muscle formation in chick embryos is initiated by migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells.
source: In chick embryos, skeletal muscle formation is initiated by migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells that trigger NOTCH signaling and myogenesis in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells, which rapidly translocate into the nascent muscle to differentiate.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a key finding of the study.

claim: Migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells trigger NOTCH signaling in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells.
source: In chick embryos, skeletal muscle formation is initiated by migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells that trigger NOTCH signaling and myogenesis in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells, which rapidly translocate into the nascent muscle to differentiate.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: NOTCH signaling triggers myogenesis in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells.
source: In chick embryos, skeletal muscle formation is initiated by migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells that trigger NOTCH signaling and myogenesis in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells, which rapidly translocate into the nascent muscle to differentiate.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental evidence in the results section.

claim: Selected epithelial somite progenitor cells rapidly translocate into the nascent muscle to differentiate.
source: In chick embryos, skeletal muscle formation is initiated by migrating Delta1-expressing neural crest cells that trigger NOTCH signaling and myogenesis in selected epithelial somite progenitor cells, which rapidly translocate into the nascent muscle to differentiate.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as part of the myogenesis process.

claim: NOTCH profoundly inhibits GSK-3β activity independent of its transcriptional function.
source: Independent of its transcriptional function, NOTCH profoundly inhibits GSK-3β activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in the results section.

claim: SNAI1 is stabilized as a result of GSK-3β inhibition by NOTCH.
source: As a result SNAI1 is stabilized, triggering an epithelial to mesenchymal transition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing SNAI1 stabilization.

claim: Stabilization of SNAI1 triggers an epithelial to mesenchymal transition.
source: As a result SNAI1 is stabilized, triggering an epithelial to mesenchymal transition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through EMT experiments.

claim: EMT allows the recruitment of β-catenin from the membrane.
source: This allows the recruitment of β-catenin from the membrane, which acts as a transcriptional co-factor to activate myogenesis, independently of WNT ligand.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with Y489F β-catenin mutant.

claim: β-catenin recruited from the membrane acts as a transcriptional co-factor to activate myogenesis.
source: This allows the recruitment of β-catenin from the membrane, which acts as a transcriptional co-factor to activate myogenesis, independently of WNT ligand.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through reporter assays and MYF5 expression analysis.

claim: β-catenin activates myogenesis independently of WNT ligand.
source: This allows the recruitment of β-catenin from the membrane, which acts as a transcriptional co-factor to activate myogenesis, independently of WNT ligand.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through DKK1 inhibition experiments.

claim: The medial border of the dermomyotome (DML) generates the first skeletal muscle cells that assemble into a primary myotome over many days of development.
source: Over many days of development, the medial border of the dermomyotome (DML) generates the first skeletal muscle cells that assemble into a primary myotome (Figure 1A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Epithelial cells in the DML either self-renew or undergo myogenic differentiation accompanied by an EMT.
source: This arises from a crucial cell fate decision: epithelial cells in the DML either self-renew or undergo myogenic differentiation and this is accompanied by an EMT that allows their translocation into the primary myotome (Denetclaw et al., 1997; Gros et al., 2009; Ordahl et al., 2001; Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: EMT allows DML cells to translocate into the primary myotome.
source: This arises from a crucial cell fate decision: epithelial cells in the DML either self-renew or undergo myogenic differentiation and this is accompanied by an EMT that allows their translocation into the primary myotome (Denetclaw et al., 1997; Gros et al., 2009; Ordahl et al., 2001; Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Signaling cues from tissues surrounding the somites act as inducers of muscle formation.
source: Classical experiments demonstrated that signaling cues from tissues surrounding the somites act as inducers of muscle formation (Ordahl and Le Douarin, 1992).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: WNT1 and WNT3a are expressed in the dorsal neural tube.
source: It was later shown that WNT1 and WNT3a are expressed in the dorsal neural tube and that, in vitro, both ligands enhance myogenesis in somites (Munsterberg et al., 1995; Stern et al., 1995; Tajbakhsh et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: WNT1 and WNT3a enhance myogenesis in somites in vitro.
source: It was later shown that WNT1 and WNT3a are expressed in the dorsal neural tube and that, in vitro, both ligands enhance myogenesis in somites (Munsterberg et al., 1995; Stern et al., 1995; Tajbakhsh et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: MYF5 promoter contains TCF binding sites required for its in vivo expression in the DML.
source: Since it was demonstrated that MYF5 promoter contains TCF binding sites required for its in vivo expression in the DML (Borello et al., 2006) and that dominant negative and constitutively active forms of TCF and β-catenin modulate MYF5 expression in somites (Abu-Elmagd et al., 2010; Gros et al., 2009), this has led to the largely accepted theory that myogenesis in somites is under the control of WNTs from the dorsal neural tube acting through a WNT/β-catenin-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Dominant negative and constitutively active forms of TCF and β-catenin modulate MYF5 expression in somites.
source: Since it was demonstrated that MYF5 promoter contains TCF binding sites required for its in vivo expression in the DML (Borello et al., 2006) and that dominant negative and constitutively active forms of TCF and β-catenin modulate MYF5 expression in somites (Abu-Elmagd et al., 2010; Gros et al., 2009), this has led to the largely accepted theory that myogenesis in somites is under the control of WNTs from the dorsal neural tube acting through a WNT/β-catenin-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Only a small proportion of DML cells initiate myogenesis at any given time despite all cells being equally exposed to WNTs.
source: This raises a paradox: although presumably all cells in the DML are equally exposed to WNTs from axial structures and are fully competent to initiate myogenesis, only a small proportion of DML cells do so at any given time (Rios et al., 2011), suggesting that other mechanisms affect the cell fate decision in selected DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The activation of MYF5 and MYOD in the DML is dependent upon the transient activation of NOTCH signaling triggered by Delta1-positive neural crest cells.
source: We recently introduced NOTCH signaling as a novel player in early myogenesis, by demonstrating that the activation of MYF5 and MYOD in the DML is dependent upon the transient activation of NOTCH signaling, triggered by Delta1-positive neural crest cells migrating from the dorsal neural tube (Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The mosaic expression of Delta1 in the migrating neural crest cell population ensures that NOTCH signaling is regularly triggered in selected DML cells.
source: Importantly, the mosaic expression of Delta1 in the migrating neural crest cell population ensures that NOTCH signaling is regularly triggered in selected DML cells, thus explaining the cell fate choice necessary to generate myotomal cells over an extended period of time, all while self-renewing the progenitor population.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an explanation for the cell fate choice mechanism.

claim: 38% of cells activating the NOTCH reporter are within the TOPflash reporter-positive population.
source: We found that, within the DML, almost half of the epithelial cells that activated the TOPflash reporter were also positive for the NOTCH reporter (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Nearly all DML cells that were positive for both NOTCH and TOPflash reporters were MYF5-positive.
source: Remarkably, nearly all DML cells that were positive for both reporters were MYF5-positive (Figure 2C), indicating a strong correlation between the activation of NOTCH and WNT reporters and the initiation of the myogenic program.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A large majority of NOTCH reporter-positive cells displayed a high TOPflash fluorescence.
source: During this analysis, we made the surprising observation that a large majority of NOTCH reporter-positive cells displayed a high TOPflash fluorescence.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on microscopy observations.

claim: Most cells that expressed low levels of TOPflash fluorescence were NOTCH-reporter negative.
source: On the contrary, most cells that expressed low levels of TOPflash fluorescence were NOTCH-reporter negative (Figure 2A,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: There is no correlation between the intensity of the TOPflash reporter and that of BFP control.
source: We found no correlation between the intensity of the TOPflash reporter and that of BFP (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The low and high levels of TOPflash fluorescence observed in DML cells are due to genuine differences in TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity.
source: This suggests that the low and high levels of TOPflash fluorescence observed in DML cells are due to genuine differences in TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the lack of correlation with BFP.

claim: The vast majority of NOTCH reporter-positive (and MYF5-positive) cells display a high TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity.
source: It confirms that the vast majority of NOTCH reporter-positive (and MYF5-positive) cells display a high TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on the analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Constitutively active β-catenin did not lead to any change in activity of the NOTCH reporter compared to controls.
source: To address this, we first co-electroporated the DML with a constitutively active form of β-catenin (Rios et al., 2010) together with the NOTCH reporter. This did not lead to any change in activity of the NOTCH reporter, compared to controls (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Co-expression of constitutively active NOTCH1 (NICD) led to rapid and robust increase in the activity of the TOPflash reporter compared to controls.
source: In contrast, the co-expression of a constitutively active form of NOTCH1 (NICD [Daudet and Lewis, 2005]) led to rapid and robust increase in the activity of the TOPflash reporter, compared to controls (Figure 3D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: CA-LEF1 co-electroporated with DN-MAML1 rescued the inhibition of MYF5 expression by DN-MAML1.
source: A constitutively active form of the most downstream effector of the WNT pathway, LEF1/TCF1 (named CA-LEF1 [Abu-Elmagd et al., 2010]), co-electroporated with DN-MAML1 not only rescued the inhibition of MYF5 expression by DN-MAML1, but also led to a strong activation of its expression that was indistinguishable from that observed after electroporation of CA-LEF1 alone (Figure 3F,G) or NICD (Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: NOTCH regulates TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity in the DML.
source: These data support the premise that NOTCH regulates TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity in the DML.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: DKK1 efficiently inhibits most, if not all TOPflash activity in the neural tube by antagonizing WNTs in the extracellular space.
source: Without DKK1, we observed a robust TOPflash reporter activity in the neural tube (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B). The co-electroporation of DKK1 abrogated nearly all reporter activity in this tissue (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). These results suggest that DKK1 efficiently inhibits most, if not all TOPflash (i.e. TCF/β-catenin transcriptional) activity in the posterior neural tube by antagonizing WNTs in the extracellular space.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the presence of DKK1, the TOPflash reporter was still active in somites.
source: We then performed a similar experiment in somites. A striking difference from the neural tube control experiment was that, even in the presence of DKK1, the TOPflash reporter was still active (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: DKK1 decreased the proportion of TOPflash reporter-positive cells by about half compared to controls.
source: While this response showed a decrease of about half in the proportion of TOPflash reporter-positive cells compared to controls (Figure 4C), remarkably nearly all cells that remained TOPflash-positive also expressed MYF5 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Nearly all cells that remained TOPflash-positive in the presence of DKK1 also expressed MYF5.
source: While this response showed a decrease of about half in the proportion of TOPflash reporter-positive cells compared to controls (Figure 4C), remarkably nearly all cells that remained TOPflash-positive also expressed MYF5 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The overall proportion of MYF5-positive cells was unaffected by DKK1.
source: As a consequence, the overall proportion of MYF5-positive cells was unaffected (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Nearly all cells that remained TOPflash-positive in the presence of DKK1 expressed the NOTCH reporter.
source: Of these cells that remained TOPflash-positive in the presence of DKK1, nearly all expressed the NOTCH reporter (Figure 4F,G), a result coherent with our observation that MYF5 is tightly associated with the activation of this reporter (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4F,G.

claim: WNT1 and DN WNT1 significantly increased or decreased, respectively, the activity of the TOPflash reporter compared to controls.
source: We observed that WNT1 and DN WNT1 significantly increased or decreased, respectively, the activity of the TOPflash reporter, compared to controls (Figure 4I–L), but importantly with no visible change to their myogenic response (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4I-L.

claim: WNT1 and DN WNT1 had no visible change to the myogenic response.
source: We observed that WNT1 and DN WNT1 significantly increased or decreased, respectively, the activity of the TOPflash reporter, compared to controls (Figure 4I–L), but importantly with no visible change to their myogenic response (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Inhibiting both DLL1 in neural crest and WNT ligands in the DML led to a near complete absence of TOPflash reporter activity in DML cells.
source: To show this, we inhibited both DLL1 in neural crest and the WNT ligands in the DML, while monitoring the activity of the TOPflash reporter and myogenesis in somites. Compared to controls (no inhibition of DLL1 in the neural crest), this led to a near complete absence of TOPflash reporter activity in DML cells (Figure 4O,P), which was now accompanied by a robust decrease in their myogenic response (Figure 4O,Q).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4O,P.

claim: Inhibiting both DLL1 in neural crest and WNT ligands in the DML was accompanied by a robust decrease in myogenic response.
source: To show this, we inhibited both DLL1 in neural crest and the WNT ligands in the DML, while monitoring the activity of the TOPflash reporter and myogenesis in somites. Compared to controls (no inhibition of DLL1 in the neural crest), this led to a near complete absence of TOPflash reporter activity in DML cells (Figure 4O,P), which was now accompanied by a robust decrease in their myogenic response (Figure 4O,Q).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4O,Q.

claim: Two distinct populations coexist in the DML: one displays strong TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity triggered by DLL1 resulting in MYF5 expression, and another shows low TOPflash reporter activity initiated by WNT ligand with no sign of myogenesis.
source: Together with the results presented in Figure 2, these data suggest that two distinct populations coexist in the DML: the first displays a strong TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity triggered by DLL1 from migrating neural crest cells, which results in the initiation of MYF5 expression. The second shows a low TOPflash reporter activity, initiated by WNT ligand transported by neural crest cells but with no sign of myogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: The initiation of myogenesis in the DML is accompanied by an EMT.
source: In the DML, the initiation of myogenesis is accompanied by an EMT (Gros et al., 2009; Rios et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: The electroporation of Y489F β-catenin resulted in a robust reduction of MYF5 expression.
source: In control embryos, we observed a normal proportion of MYF5-positive DML cells (Figure 5A,C). In contrast, the electroporation of Y489F β-catenin resulted in a robust reduction of MYF5 expression (Figure 5B,C), suggesting that junctional β-catenin is required for the early activation of myogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Junctional β-catenin is required for the early activation of myogenesis.
source: In control embryos, we observed a normal proportion of MYF5-positive DML cells (Figure 5A,C). In contrast, the electroporation of Y489F β-catenin resulted in a robust reduction of MYF5 expression (Figure 5B,C), suggesting that junctional β-catenin is required for the early activation of myogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the Y489F β-catenin experiment.

claim: The induction of NICD expression resulted in a robust increase in overall β-catenin protein levels in electroporated cells.
source: In control embryos, the induction of NICD expression resulted in a robust increase in overall (nuclear and cytoplasmic) β-catenin protein levels in electroporated cells (as determined by immunostaining for the Myc tag present on the exogenous WT β-catenin as well as by staining for endogenous β-catenin [Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2]).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The vast majority of NICD+/WT β-catenin+ cells expressed MYF5.
source: In these embryos, the vast majority of NICD+/WT β-catenin+ cells expressed MYF5 as expected (Figure 5E,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5E,G.

claim: The presence of Y489F β-catenin prevented the activation of myogenesis by NICD.
source: The myogenic response in embryos electroporated with Y489F β-catenin was strikingly different, and the presence of the mutant form of β-catenin not only prevented the activation of myogenesis by NICD, but also resulted in a dramatic reduction of MYF5 expression (Figure 5F,G) that was similar to the decrease observed when Y489F β-catenin was electroporated alone (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: Y489F β-catenin remained mainly distributed at the membrane and AJ of DML cells.
source: As reported (Rhee et al., 2007), Y489F β-catenin remained mainly distributed at the membrane and AJ of DML cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), suggesting that it did not mobilize from the junctional complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The pool of β-catenin at the AJ and along the plasma membrane of DML cells acts as a reservoir for the NOTCH-mediated, strong β-catenin-dependent response required for the activation of MYF5.
source: Together with the observation that MYF5 expression is associated with high activity of the TOPflash reporter in DML cells (Figures 2 and 4), our data suggest that the pool of β-catenin at the AJ and along the plasma membrane of DML cells acts as a reservoir for the NOTCH-mediated, strong β-catenin-dependent response required for the activation of MYF5.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: SNAI1 is expressed in the epithelial dermomyotome, including the DML.
source: In early chick embryos, SNAI1 is expressed in the epithelial dermomyotome, including the DML.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: SNAI1 activation leads to the down-regulation of N-cadherin expression in epithelial cells located in the central dermomyotome and to their subsequent EMT.
source: Its activation leads to the down-regulation of N-cadherin expression present at the adherens junction of epithelial cells located in the central dermomyotome and to their subsequent EMT (Delfini et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The over-expression of SNAI1 in the DML induced a significant increase in the translocation of DML cells into the myotome.
source: Coherent with this, the over-expression of SNAI1 in the DML induced a significant increase in the translocation of DML cells into the myotome (Figure 6A,B), while the inhibition of its function by a SNAI1-specific siRNA (Delfini et al., 2009) inhibited their translocation (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: The inhibition of SNAI1 function by a SNAI1-specific siRNA inhibited the translocation of DML cells into the myotome.
source: Coherent with this, the over-expression of SNAI1 in the DML induced a significant increase in the translocation of DML cells into the myotome (Figure 6A,B), while the inhibition of its function by a SNAI1-specific siRNA (Delfini et al., 2009) inhibited their translocation (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: The electroporation of SNAI1 in the DML induced a strong activation of MYF5 expression compared to controls.
source: The electroporation of SNAI1 in the DML induced a strong activation of MYF5 expression, compared to controls (Figure 6F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6F,G.

claim: The electroporation of a dominant-negative form of SNAIL-1 or an siRNA directed against SNAI1 resulted in a significant decrease in MYF5 expression.
source: Conversely, the electroporation of a dominant-negative form of SNAIL-1 or an siRNA directed against SNAI1 (Delfini et al., 2009) resulted in a significant decrease in MYF5 expression (Figure 6C,E,F,G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6C,E,F,G.

claim: The massive increase in MYF5 expression observed after NICD expression was profoundly reduced by DN-SNAI1.
source: Finally, we co-electroporated NICD together with the dominant-negative form of SNAI1 and observed that the massive increase in MYF5 expression observed after NICD expression (Rios et al., 2011) was profoundly reduced by DN-SNAI1 (Figure 6F,G), thus demonstrating that SNAI1 activation is a necessary step, downstream of NOTCH, in the chain of events that leads to the activation of MYF5 in DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6F,G.

claim: SNAI1 activation is a necessary step, downstream of NOTCH, in the chain of events that leads to the activation of MYF5 in DML cells.
source: Finally, we co-electroporated NICD together with the dominant-negative form of SNAI1 and observed that the massive increase in MYF5 expression observed after NICD expression (Rios et al., 2011) was profoundly reduced by DN-SNAI1 (Figure 6F,G), thus demonstrating that SNAI1 activation is a necessary step, downstream of NOTCH, in the chain of events that leads to the activation of MYF5 in DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: SNAI1 protein has a short half-life, estimated to be about 25 min.
source: Due to this continuous degradation, SNAI1 protein has a short half-life, estimated to be about 25 min (Zhou et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The co-electroporation of NICD with SNAI1-GFP led to a massive increase in GFP staining in most electroporated cells.
source: In control embryos, GFP was undetectable under UV examination, but faintly visible after immunostaining and confocal examination in electroporated cells (Figure 7A). In sharp contrast, the co-electroporation of NICD with SNAI1-GFP led to a massive increase in GFP staining in most electroporated cells (Figure 7A), suggesting that the activation of NOTCH signaling prevents the degradation of SNAI1 that normally occurs in DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The activation of NOTCH signaling prevents the degradation of SNAI1 that normally occurs in DML cells.
source: In control embryos, GFP was undetectable under UV examination, but faintly visible after immunostaining and confocal examination in electroporated cells (Figure 7A). In sharp contrast, the co-electroporation of NICD with SNAI1-GFP led to a massive increase in GFP staining in most electroporated cells (Figure 7A), suggesting that the activation of NOTCH signaling prevents the degradation of SNAI1 that normally occurs in DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the SNAI1-GFP experiment.

claim: Fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor was only detected in a small proportion of electroporated DML cells under normal, unperturbed conditions.
source: We first determined whether the GSK-3β biosensor is active in DML cells, and observed that fluorescence of the biosensor was only detected in a small proportion of electroporated DML cells (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In the majority of DML cells under normal, unperturbed conditions, GSK-3β is active.
source: This observation indicates that in the majority of DML cells under normal, unperturbed conditions, GSK-3β is active (i.e. low or no biosensor detectable).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the biosensor data.

claim: In a minority of DML cells, GSK-3β is inhibited.
source: However, in a minority of cells, GSK-3β is inhibited (i.e. high level of biosensor).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the biosensor data.

claim: The cells in which the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor is observed are those that activate the NOTCH reporter.
source: To find out the identity of the biosensor-positive cells in normal, unperturbed condition, we performed a series of co-electroporations followed by immunostaining. This showed that the cells in which the fluorescence of the biosensor is observed are those that i) activate the NOTCH reporter (Figure 7C,D), ii) in which SNAI1 is active (Figure 7F,G) and iii) are MYF5-positive (Figure 7C,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The cells in which the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor is observed are those in which SNAI1 is active.
source: To find out the identity of the biosensor-positive cells in normal, unperturbed condition, we performed a series of co-electroporations followed by immunostaining. This showed that the cells in which the fluorescence of the biosensor is observed are those that i) activate the NOTCH reporter (Figure 7C,D), ii) in which SNAI1 is active (Figure 7F,G) and iii) are MYF5-positive (Figure 7C,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7F,G.

claim: The cells in which the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor is observed are those that are MYF5-positive.
source: To find out the identity of the biosensor-positive cells in normal, unperturbed condition, we performed a series of co-electroporations followed by immunostaining. This showed that the cells in which the fluorescence of the biosensor is observed are those that i) activate the NOTCH reporter (Figure 7C,D), ii) in which SNAI1 is active (Figure 7F,G) and iii) are MYF5-positive (Figure 7C,E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7C,E.

claim: Co-electroporating the GSK-3β biosensor together with NICD resulted in a massive increase in the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor.
source: We then tested whether NOTCH regulates GSK-3β by co-electroporating the biosensor together with NICD. This resulted in a massive increase in the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor (Figure 7B), suggesting that NICD inhibits GSK-3β kinase activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: NICD inhibits GSK-3β kinase activity.
source: We then tested whether NOTCH regulates GSK-3β by co-electroporating the biosensor together with NICD. This resulted in a massive increase in the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor (Figure 7B), suggesting that NICD inhibits GSK-3β kinase activity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the biosensor experiment.

claim: Electroporating DLL1 in the neural crest cell population resulted in a strong increase in the fluorescence of the GSK-3β biosensor in somites compared to controls.
source: To eliminate the possibility that the increase in fluorescence of the biosensor was due to a non-physiological effect of NICD expression in DML cells, we induced the activation of NOTCH signaling in the DML by electroporating DLL1 in the neural crest cell population (as described in Figure 4H), with the GSK-3β biosensor electroporated in adjacent somites. Again, we observed a strong increase in the fluorescence of the biosensor in somites when compared to controls (Figure 7H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7H,I.

claim: The electroporation of a dominant-negative form of GSK-3β mimicked the effects of NOTCH activation on SNAI1 and MYF5.
source: The electroporation of a dominant-negative form of GSK-3β (DN-GSK-3β [Taelman et al., 2010]) mimicked the effects of NOTCH activation on SNAI1 and MYF5, resulting in a significant increase in the proportion of DML cells undergoing EMT (Figure 7J,K) as well as a robust increase in MYF5 expression in DML cells (Figure 7L).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7J-L.

claim: A direct consequence of the activation of NOTCH signaling by migrating DLL1-positive neural crest cells is an inhibition of GSK-3β activity that leads to a stabilization of the SNAI1 protein, which triggers an EMT of DML cells.
source: Altogether our data suggest that a direct consequence of the activation of NOTCH signaling by migrating DLL1-positive neural crest cells is an inhibition of GSK-3β activity that leads to a stabilization of the SNAI1 protein, which triggers an EMT of DML cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: DN-RBPJ and CA-RBPJ significantly inhibited or activated the NOTCH reporter, respectively, compared to controls.
source: As expected, the DN-RBPJ and CA-RBPJ significantly inhibited or activated the NOTCH reporter, respectively, compared to controls (Figure 8A–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 8A-D.

claim: DN-RBPJ and CA-RBPJ failed to modify the expression of MYF5 in the DML compared to controls.
source: However, both constructs failed to modify the expression of MYF5 in this structure, compared to controls (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 8E.

claim: NICD regulates myogenesis in the DML independently of its transcriptional activity with RBPJ.
source: These results indicate that NICD regulates myogenesis in the DML independently of its transcriptional activity with RBPJ.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the RBPJ experiments.

claim: CD4-NICD did not enter the nucleus and did not activate the NOTCH reporter.
source: Unlike wild-type NICD, which upon electroporation readily enters the nucleus and massively activates the NOTCH reporter (Rios et al., 2011), immunostaining for CD4-NICD was not observed in the nucleus and, coherent with this, it did not activate the NOTCH reporter (Figure 9A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 9A,B.

claim: CD4-NICD expression resulted in a massive stabilization of the GSK-3β biosensor that was indistinguishable from that obtained after electroporation of NICD.
source: Despite this, CD4-NICD expression resulted in a massive stabilization of the GSK-3β biosensor that was indistinguishable from that obtained after electroporation of NICD (Figure 9C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 9C,D.

claim: The regulation of GSK-3β activity by CD4-NICD is not a transcriptional response to NOTCH signaling.
source: This suggests that the regulation of GSK-3β activity by CD4-NICD is not a transcriptional response to NOTCH signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the CD4-NICD experiment.

claim: The electroporation of CD4-NICD led to a massive stabilization of SNAI1 protein comparable to NICD alone.
source: Indeed, we observed that the electroporation of CD4-NICD led to i) a massive stabilization of SNAI1 protein comparable to NICD alone (Figure 9E,F) and ii) to a robust increase of MYF5 expression in DML cells, not significantly different from the NICD alone (Figure 9G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 9E,F.

claim: The electroporation of CD4-NICD led to a robust increase of MYF5 expression in DML cells, not significantly different from NICD alone.
source: Indeed, we observed that the electroporation of CD4-NICD led to i) a massive stabilization of SNAI1 protein comparable to NICD alone (Figure 9E,F) and ii) to a robust increase of MYF5 expression in DML cells, not significantly different from the NICD alone (Figure 9G,H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 9G,H.

claim: The activation of MYF5 in DML cells is the result of a cytoplasmic function of NICD that can be uncoupled from its role as a transcriptional co-activator in the nucleus.
source: These data demonstrate that the activation of MYF5 in DML cells is the result of a cytoplasmic function of NICD that can be uncoupled from its role as a transcriptional co-activator in the nucleus.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the CD4-NICD experiments.

claim: The signaling module uncovered integrates cell fate determination and epithelial plasticity.
source: The findings presented here uncover a unique signaling module, triggered by a signal presented by migrating neural crest cells to selected progenitors in the somites. This signal is transduced into two distinct, but interrelated outcomes i) a cell fate decision in the receiving cells that leads to their entry into the myogenic program and ii) an EMT that allows their translocation into the myotome (Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a summary of the findings.

claim: EMT is intimately associated with essential changes in cell specification in many developmental processes.
source: EMT is intimately associated with essential changes in cell specification in many developmental processes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as general knowledge.

claim: The signaling module targets GSK-3β, the main regulator of SNAI1 stability.
source: A remarkable aspect of the signaling module described here is that it targets GSK-3β, the main regulator of SNAI1 stability.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a key feature of the mechanism.

claim: Aiming at GSK-3β may protect the β-catenin released during the EMT process from degradation.
source: In addition, aiming at GSK-3β may protect the β-catenin released during the EMT process from degradation, allowing it to accumulate sufficiently to act as a transcriptional co-factor, thereby resulting in a quasi-automatic coupling of EMT and β-catenin-dependent cell fate changes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The same signaling circuitry could couple EMT to cell fate decisions in a wide variety of epithelia in normal and pathological conditions.
source: Given the commonality of the key players described here in this paper, it is plausible that the same signaling circuitry could couple EMT to cell fate decisions in a wide variety of epithelia in normal and pathological conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a speculation about broader implications.

claim: Cytosolic interactions of NICD with various molecular partners that result in cellular responses independent of RBPJ have been described in in vitro experimental settings.
source: However, cytosolic interactions of NICD with various molecular partners that result in cellular responses independent of RBPJ, have been described in in vitro experimental settings (reviewed in [Andersen et al., 2014; Ayaz and Osborne, 2014]), but also in Drosophila (Le Gall et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The data uncover a novel in vivo function of NOTCH1 that takes place in the cytosol and leads to GSK-3β inhibition.
source: Our data uncover a novel in vivo function of NOTCH1 that takes place in the cytosol and leads to GSK-3β inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a key finding.

claim: The transcriptional activity of NICD is modified by its phosphorylation in vitro, probably by GSK-3β.
source: It was shown that the transcriptional activity of NICD is modified by its phosphorylation in vitro, probably by GSK-3β (Espinosa et al., 2003; Foltz et al., 2002; Schweisguth, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The response observed results from a titration of GSK-3β kinase activity by NICD that is amplified by the stabilization of SNAI, itself a substrate for this kinase.
source: A hypothesis is that the response we observed results from a titration of GSK-3β kinase activity by NICD that is amplified by the stabilization of SNAI, itself a substrate for this kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a hypothesis.

claim: Changes in the transcriptional activity of β-catenin have been associated with the disassembly of the junctional complex at the plasma membrane in vitro.
source: While it is largely accepted that β-catenin participates in adhesion and signaling functions in a mutually exclusive manner, changes in the transcriptional activity of β-catenin have also been associated with the disassembly of the junctional complex at the plasma membrane in vitro (Brembeck et al., 2006; Gavard and Mège, 2012; Nelson and Nusse, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The results provide direct evidence that the pool of β-catenin accumulated at the membrane and/or at the AJ has important signaling functions in addition to its established role in cell-cell adhesion in vivo.
source: The results reported here provide direct evidence that this is also the case in vivo and demonstrate that the pool of β-catenin accumulated at the membrane and/or at the AJ has important signaling functions in addition to its established role in cell-cell adhesion.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a key finding.

claim: Distinct thresholds of TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity are associated with discrete cellular outputs.
source: Remarkably, we observed distinct thresholds of TCF/β-catenin transcriptional activity associated with discrete cellular outputs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as an observation.

claim: WNT(s) expressed by the dorsal neural tube and transported by neural crest cells regulate the expression of WNT11 in the DML through canonical WNT signaling.
source: It is known that WNT(s) expressed by the dorsal neural tube and transported by neural crest cells regulate the expression of WNT11 in the DML through canonical WNT signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as established knowledge.

claim: WNT11 plays an essential role in the oriented elongation of early muscle fibers through planar cell polarity signaling.
source: WNT11 itself plays an essential role in the oriented elongation of early muscle fibers through planar cell polarity signaling (Gros et al., 2009; Marcelle et al., 1997; Serralbo and Marcelle, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The WNTs carried by neural crest cells induce a low TOPflash response that regulates myotome's organization, but has no influence on MYF5 expression.
source: The data presented here suggest that the WNTs carried by neural crest cells induce a low TOPflash response that regulates myotome's organization, but has no influence on MYF5 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: DLL1, via the signaling module uncovered, provokes the release of junctional β-catenin that leads to a high TOPflash response sufficient to trigger myogenesis.
source: On the contrary, DLL1, via the signaling module uncovered here, provokes the release of junctional β-catenin that leads to a high TOPflash response sufficient to trigger myogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: β-catenin phosphorylated at the AJ on Y489 is transported into the nucleus and is transcriptionally active in vitro.
source: Rhee and colleagues have shown that β-catenin phosphorylated at the AJ on Y489 is transported into the nucleus and is transcriptionally active in vitro (Rhee et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: The NOTCH signal is a permissive one, while the instructive role is executed by β-catenin and TCF/LEF.
source: The necessary function of NOTCH in this process (Rios et al., 2011) is confirmed, but the present work demonstrates that the NOTCH signal is a permissive one, while the instructive role is executed by β-catenin and TCF/LEF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section as a conclusion from the study.
